To: priya_natarajan@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-22 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: High latency + 500s from reserved pool (URGENT)

Priya —

We started seeing sustained tail latency spikes and increased 500 errors from our reserved capacity starting ~08:30 PT. P95 token latency jumped from ~180ms to 1.6s and error rate rose to ~4.8% for two of our high-throughput endpoints. This is causing request timeouts in our downstream processing and we have customers impacted.

We've attached a short CSV with the SLO metrics and the raw support logs showing repeated "pool capacity exceeded" errors and long queue times.

Key context:
- Region: us-west-2 (reserved pool rb-qs-2)
- Model: qbank-2b-longcontext (pinned)
- Traffic: steady high-concurrency inference from reconciliation jobs (many long-context requests)

Can you confirm a mitigation path? Is Redwood auto-fallback to a quantized variant active? We need an ETA on relief and whether you can route heavy tails to a hosted fallback.

Thanks,
Aisha Verma
Senior SRE, QuantaBank

On 2027-05-22 09:21, priya_natarajan@redwood.com wrote:
> Team — forwarding the QuantaBank alert.

Quick triage notes from infra:
- We see steady queue depth growth on rb-qs-2 between 08:18-08:45 PT tied to multiple concurrent long-context sessions (context lengths > 12k).
- KV cache hit-rate dropped ~22% coincident with queue growth; kernel scheduling shows repeated preemption on the highest-priority lane.
- Several requests timed out waiting for new worker allocation; autoscaler is at its burst ceiling for that pool.

Immediate mitigations we can take (30–90min):
- Toggle temporary routing to a hosted-compatible quantized variant (qbank-2b-q4) for non-latency-sensitive reconciliation routes. Requires policy change and customer consent.
- Increase burst cap on rb-qs-2 by +3 nodes (if Vivek approves emergency capacity). This will cost ~$1.8k/hr but will restore headroom.
- Enable aggressive prefix caching for repeated reconciliation prompts (config change; low risk).

I'll attach a short diagnostics dump. If autoscaler remains pinned we'll need manual pool resizes.

[attachment: diagnostic_snippet_pool_metrics.txt]

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Infra Lead, Serving Runtime

Thanks for the heads up and the logs. We're trigging an ops bridge now (invite attached). Short summary of what we're doing immediately:
1) We recommend routing the reconciliation job traffic for the next 2hrs to qbank-2b-q4 (quantized) for non-real-time batches — this will cut per-token latency and reduce pressure on the reserved pool. Marcus will coordinate the routing change.
2) We're requesting emergency burst capacity (+3 nodes) for rb-qs-2 to provide immediate headroom while routing is in progress.
3) We're applying an aggressive prefix caching rule to the reconciliation routes to lower repeated compute.

I'll be on the bridge and will keep you updated every 15 minutes. Apologies for the disruption — we're prioritizing restoring your SLOs.

Calendar: https://zoom.us/j/879201938 (bridge at 10:00 PT).

—Marissa Cole
